newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Peasants want 2 pct import tax after flood.
newsitem.headline: Polish Peasants want 2 pct import tax after flood.

text.p: The Polish Peasant Party (PSL), the smaller group in the ruling leftist coalition, called on Friday for a two-percent tax on all imported goods to help finance reconstruction of flood-hit areas.

"We put forward a plan to introduce a border import tax amounting to two percent. Nobody should have any doubts that the flood justifies special measures," PSL spokesman Aleksander Bentkowski told a news conference.
He said the tax would contribute an additional 2.8 billion zlotys annually to the national budget.
Officials of the government and the coalition's second group, the ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD), were not immediately available for comment on the proposal.

The government wants to finance its relief programme for the victims of the flood, which killed 55 people and swamped some 6,000 sq km in southern Poland, by reallocating funds in this year's budget, and borrowing from the central bank and abroad.
Poland moved to scrap a three-percent import tax this year, a step enforced by Poland's entry to the Organisation for European Cooperation and Development (OECD).
